cases.sentence: И я тебе говорил и говорю: – нехорошо, что ты не ездишь на собрания и вообще устранился от ___.
cases.explain: «земского дела» — after the preposition «от», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “Do you know, I’ve been thinking about you,” said Sergey Ivanovitch. “It’s beyond everything what’s being done in the district, according to what this doctor tells me. He’s a very intelligent fellow. And as I’ve told you before, I tell you again: it’s not right for you not to go to the meetings, and altogether to keep out of the district business. If decent people won’t go into it, of course it’s bound to go all wrong. We pay the money, and it all goes in salaries, and there are no schools, nor district nurses, nor midwives, nor drugstores—nothing.”

cases.sentence: Если ___ будут удаляться, разумеется, все пойдет бог знает как.
cases.explain: «порядочные люди» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Do you know, I’ve been thinking about you,” said Sergey Ivanovitch. “It’s beyond everything what’s being done in the district, according to what this doctor tells me. If decent people won’t go into it, of course it’s bound to go all wrong. We pay the money, and it all goes in salaries, and there are no schools, nor district nurses, nor midwives, nor drugstores—nothing.”

cases.sentence: Но тут надо быть убежденным прежде, что нужно иметь ___ для этих дел и, главное, в том, что все эти дела важны очень.
cases.explain: «известные способности» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “Self-respect!” said Levin, stung to the quick by his brother’s words; “I don’t understand. If they’d told me at college that other people understood the integral calculus, and I didn’t, then pride would have come in. But in this case one wants first to be convinced that one has certain qualifications for this sort of business, and especially that all this business is of great importance.”

cases.sentence: – Ну, послушай, однако, – нахмурив свое красивое умное лицо, сказал ___, – есть границы всему.
cases.explain: «старший брат» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Come, really though,” said the elder brother, with a frown on his handsome, clever face, “there’s a limit to everything. It’s very well to be original and genuine, and to dislike everything conventional—I know all about that; but really, what you’re saying either has no meaning, or it has a very wrong meaning. How can you think it a matter of no importance whether the peasant, whom you love as you assert. …”

cases.sentence: Это очень хорошо быть чудаком и искренним человеком и не любить фальшь, – я все это знаю; но ведь то, что ты говоришь, или не имеет смысла, или имеет очень ___.
cases.explain: «дурной смысл» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “Come, really though,” said the elder brother, with a frown on his handsome, clever face, “there’s a limit to everything. It’s very well to be original and genuine, and to dislike everything conventional—I know all about that; but really, what you’re saying either has no meaning, or it has a very wrong meaning. How can you think it a matter of no importance whether the peasant, whom you love as you assert. …”

cases.sentence: ___ замаривают детей, и народ коснеет в невежестве и остается во власти всякого писаря, а тебе дано в руки средство помочь этому, и ты не помогаешь, потому что, по-твоему, это не важно.
cases.explain: «Грубые бабки» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “… dies without help? The ignorant peasant-women starve the children, and the people stagnate in darkness, and are helpless in the hands of every village clerk, while you have at your disposal a means of helping them, and don’t help them because to your mind it’s of no importance.”

cases.sentence: Константин Левин чувствовал, что ему остается только покориться или признаться в недостатке любви к ___.
cases.explain: «общему делу» — after the preposition «к», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: Konstantin Levin felt that there was no course open to him but to submit, or to confess to a lack of zeal for the public good. And this mortified him and hurt his feelings.

cases.sentence: Константин Левин чувствовал себя нравственно припертым к стене и потому разгорячился и высказал невольно главную причину своего равнодушия к ___.
cases.explain: «общему делу» — after the preposition «к», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: Konstantin Levin felt himself morally pinned against a wall, and so he got hot, and unconsciously blurted out the chief cause of his indifference to public business.

cases.sentence: Сергея Ивановича на минуту удивило это ___ на дело; но он тотчас составил новый план атаки.
cases.explain: «неожиданное воззрение» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Sergey Ivanovitch was for a minute surprised at this unexpected view of the subject; but he promptly made a new plan of attack. He was silent for a little, drew out a hook, threw it in again, and turned to his brother smiling.

cases.sentence: Потом ___, работник тебе же нужнее и дороже.
cases.explain: «грамотный мужик» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “That remains to be proved. … Next, the peasant who can read and write is as a workman of more use and value to you.”

cases.sentence: – Если ты признаешь это благом, – сказал Сергей Иванович, – то ты, как ___, не можешь не любить и не сочувствовать такому делу и потому не желать работать для него.
cases.explain: «честный человек» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “If you admit that it is a benefit,” said Sergey Ivanovitch, “then, as an honest man, you cannot help caring about it and sympathizing with the movement, and so wishing to work for it.”

cases.sentence: Нет, уж если мы разговорились, то объясни мне с ___ зрения, – сказал Левин.
cases.explain: «философской точки» — after the preposition «с», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “No; since we are talking, explain it to me from the philosophical point of view,” said Levin.

cases.sentence: Теперь в ___ я, как дворянин, не вижу ничего, что бы содействовало моему благосостоянию.
cases.explain: «земских учреждениях» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: “I’ll tell you, then,” he said with heat, “I imagine the mainspring of all our actions is, after all, self-interest. Now in the local institutions I, as a nobleman, see nothing that could conduce to my prosperity, and the roads are not better and could not be better; my horses carry me well enough over bad ones. Doctors and dispensaries are no use to me. An arbitrator of disputes is no use to me. I never appeal to him, and never shall appeal to him. The schools are no good to me, but positively harmful, as I told you. For me the district institutions simply mean the liability to pay fourpence halfpenny for every three acres, to drive into the town, sleep with bugs, and listen to all sorts of idiocy and loathsomeness, and self-interest offers me no inducement.”

cases.sentence: Для меня земские учреждения просто повинность платить восемнадцать копеек с десятины, ездить в город, ночевать с клопами и слушать всякий вздор и гадости, а ___ меня не побуждает.
cases.explain: «личный интерес» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “I’ll tell you, then,” he said with heat, “I imagine the mainspring of all our actions is, after all, self-interest. Now in the local institutions I, as a nobleman, see nothing that could conduce to my prosperity, and the roads are not better and could not be better; my horses carry me well enough over bad ones. Doctors and dispensaries are no use to me. An arbitrator of disputes is no use to me. I never appeal to him, and never shall appeal to him. The schools are no good to me, but positively harmful, as I told you. For me the district institutions simply mean the liability to pay fourpence halfpenny for every three acres, to drive into the town, sleep with bugs, and listen to all sorts of idiocy and loathsomeness, and self-interest offers me no inducement.”

cases.sentence: – Позволь, – перебил с улыбкой Сергей Иванович, – ___ не побуждал нас работать для освобождения крестьян, а мы работали.
cases.explain: «личный интерес» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Excuse me,” Sergey Ivanovitch interposed with a smile, “self-interest did not induce us to work for the emancipation of the serfs, but we did work for it.”

cases.sentence: – Нет! – все более горячась, перебил Константин. – Освобождение крестьян было ___.
cases.explain: «другое дело» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “No!” Konstantin Levin broke in with still greater heat; “the emancipation of the serfs was a different matter. There self-interest did come in. One longed to throw off that yoke that crushed us, all decent people among us. But to be a town councilor and discuss how many dustmen are needed, and how chimneys shall be constructed in the town in which I don’t live—to serve on a jury and try a peasant who’s stolen a flitch of bacon, and listen for six hours at a stretch to all sorts of jabber from the counsel for the defense and the prosecution, and the president cross-examining my old half-witted Alioshka, ‘Do you admit, prisoner in the dock, the fact of the removal of the bacon?’ ‘Eh?’ ”

cases.sentence: Но Константину Левину хотелось оправдаться в том недостатке, который он знал за собой, в равнодушии к ___, и он продолжал.
cases.explain: «общему благу» — after the preposition «к», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: But Konstantin Levin wanted to justify himself for the failing, of which he was conscious, of lack of zeal for the public welfare, and he went on.

cases.sentence: – Я думаю, – сказал Константин, – что никакая деятельность не может быть прочна, – если она не имеет основы в ___.
cases.explain: «личном интересе» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: “I imagine,” he said, “that no sort of activity is likely to be lasting if it is not founded on self-interest, that’s a universal principle, a philosophical principle,” he said, repeating the word “philosophical” with determination, as though wishing to show that he had as much right as anyone else to talk of philosophy.

cases.sentence: Это ___, философская, – сказал он, с решительностью повторяя слово философская, как будто желая показать, что он тоже имеет право, как и всякий, говорить о философии.
cases.explain: «общая истина» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “I imagine,” he said, “that no sort of activity is likely to be lasting if it is not founded on self-interest, that’s a universal principle, a philosophical principle,” he said, repeating the word “philosophical” with determination, as though wishing to show that he had as much right as anyone else to talk of philosophy.

cases.sentence: – Ну, уж о философии ты оставь, – сказал он. – ___ философии всех веков состоит именно в том, чтобы найти ту необходимую связь, которая существует между личным интересом и общим.
cases.explain: «Главная задача» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Come, you’d better let philosophy alone,” he said. “The chief problem of the philosophy of all ages consists just in finding the indispensable connection which exists between individual and social interests. But that’s not to the point; what is to the point is a correction I must make in your comparison. The birches are not simply stuck in, but some are sown and some are planted, and one must deal carefully with them. It’s only those peoples that have an intuitive sense of what’s of importance and significance in their institutions, and know how to value them, that have a future before them—it’s only those peoples that one can truly call historical.”

cases.sentence: – Ну, уж о философии ты оставь, – сказал он. – Главная задача философии всех веков состоит именно в том, чтобы найти ту необходимую связь, которая существует между ___ и общим.
cases.explain: «личным интересом» — after the preposition «между», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.

But that’s not to the point; what is to the point is a correction I must make in your comparison. The birches are not simply stuck in, but some are sown and some are planted, and one must deal carefully with them. It’s only those peoples that have an intuitive sense of what’s of importance and significance in their institutions, and know how to value them, that have a future before them—it’s only those peoples that one can truly call historical.”

cases.sentence: – Что же касается до того, что тебе это не нравится, то, извини меня, – это наша русская лень и барство, а я уверен, что у тебя это ___, и пройдет.
cases.explain: «временное заблуждение» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “As for your dislike of it, excuse my saying so, that’s simply our Russian sloth and old serf-owner’s ways, and I’m convinced that in you it’s a temporary error and will pass.”
